titleAttr: Subject: Reduced SHIP Supportive Services Funding Request for Mark-Up From: Commissioner Ann To: Judge Brown, Commissioner Travillion, Commissioner Shea, and Commissioner Morales Date: September 9, 2026 ________________________________________________________________________________ Purpose: This memo updates the SHIP supportive service funding request (BH-02). Reduced Funding Request: Instead of $4.6M, we only need $2.0M in ongoing funding and $0 in one-time funding. This smaller request is the result of the conversations we have had with The City of Austin and the St. David’s Foundation about leveraging each other’s funding. · Leverage Opportunity: o St. David’s Foundation (SDF): Per CEO Ed Burger’s letter, SDF’s Board will be voting on September 15th to approve a one-time $6.0M grant (to be spent over two years) for SHIP supportive services. This grant, if approved, is a one-time investment to “allow local government leaders to create a sustainable public funding model for the services component of PSH.” o City of Austin: Per T.C. Broadnax and David Gray’s letter, “we [the City of Austin] are willing to support SHIP supportive services as a partner, while recognizing that Travis County is well positioned to lead this particular investment…” · City and County Jointly Award to 2 SHIP projects: Using a previous earmark for PSH, County HHS partnered with the City to fund $1.3M for support services annually for the next five years. Contingent on Court approval, this award will reduce the SHIP PSH support service request to $3.8M in FY27 and $8.6M in FY28. Building a Diversion to Housing Pipeline We know that over 50% of our jail population suffers from mental illness also experiences homelessness. PSH will disrupt the cycle of jail and homelessness by providing people with stable housing and access to ongoing healthcare. Based on recent conversations with ECHO and the City of Austin, we will jointly create a pathway from our diversion pilot (and other diversion programs) to the housing our clients’ desperately need.

titleAttr: Greetings - Attached is an update to the LFRF proposal for diversion services, bridge housing and data sharing. Let's work out the details and get started. And then, assess and iterate to build a system of services that provides the right care, in the right place, at the right time, so that we prevent and reduce unnecessary jail time. Experiences from the pilot - learning what works here and what doesn't will be invaluable as we anticipate colocating jail diversion services with a new central booking facility. Also, I'm encouraged and grateful that Integral Care has proposed enhancing emergency psychiatric services and pivoting other resources to get us started; City Council passed a resolution to find financial resources necessary to partner on the pilot; Central Health has sent a letter of financial/heatlhcare support and the Downtown Austin Alliance spoke out early in support. I've inititated conversations with hospitals and private philanthropy and believe that our leadership and financial committment will be key to building the partnerships needed for success. I look forward to our discussions. Ann Howard, Precinct 3 Commissioner

anchor: From Commissioner Shea, re: ARPA funds
titleAttr: As we approach our next Court discussion on ARPA funds, I'd like to share a few comments on how I'm thinking about it: 1. I want to focus on building back better, particularly by improving the resilience of those most impacted by climate change, which is disproportionately low-income communities. 2. I support exploring a participatory budgeting process for a portion of our ARPA funds, specifically for programmatic investments intended to improve the quality of life of Travis County residents. 3. I am committed to expending ARPA funds in a fiscally responsible manner, and it would not be fiscally responsible to deviate from the Financial and Debt Policies of the Travis County Commissioner’s Court, which states that “The County’s goal is to only use permanent revenue sources for on-going, permanent expenses. This means that one-time revenue sources (including ending fund balance) will not be used for on-going commitments. Temporary revenues are intended to be used solely for temporary expenses." This is one of the long-standing principles, traditions and practices which have guided the County and have helped maintain financial stability over many years. 4. I remain constantly mindful that unlike municipalities, which have diverse revenue streams, counties are almost solely dependent on property taxes. Furthermore, in 2019 the Texas Legislature imposed a 3.5% cap on Travis County’s ability to increase that revenue stream. As a result, Travis County is already in a struggle to identify sufficient ongoing funding for existing commitments (including, but not limited to, the full $13M+ annual cost of operating the Public Defender Office once the TIDC grant ends, and necessary increases to maintain existing efforts in all of the various direct social services Travis County provides to prevent residents from entering the homelessness pipeline). I understand that tomorrow's agenda item is narrowly focused on how to structure the community engagement process for a to-be-determined portion of our ARPA funds. I am looking forward to that discussion but wanted to also provide a broader framework of how I'm approaching the considerable responsibility of being a part of the decision-making process for this incredible investment in our community.
